draft.answer:
No. Take the nonnegative integer n=40. Then
n^2+n+41=40^2+40+41=1681=41·41.
Since 1<41<1681, this is a nontrivial factorization, so the value is composite. Hence n=40 is a counterexample, and the statement is false.
